title: Responder Briefcase: compact incident summaries with decision traces and actionable snapshots
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Problem: On-call responders currently open multiple panels (alert details, runbook, cost dashboard, incident timeline) to form a decision about mitigation steps. This is slow under pressure and loses context for postmortem capture.

Goal: Design a compact "responder briefcase" surface — a slim, focused drawer that bundles an incident summary, recent decisions (decision traces), one-click action affordances (runbooks / rollback / route-to-fallback), and a postmortem capture link. It must surface cost implications of suggested actions and a clear final-state indicator for handoffs.

This ticket covers: low-fidelity -> high-fidelity prototype, microcopy, accessibility checks, and a short usability test with 6 SRE/Platform engineers. Deliverables: Figma prototype, annotated flow, acceptance criteria, and a small front-end spec for Console engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Briefcase opens from alert header and docks to right side without obscuring timeline
Shows top-3 decisions (what, who, when) with inline rationale snippets and links to evidence (logs/metrics)
Includes action buttons: Runbook | Route-to-Fallback | Trigger-Playbook | Capture-Postmortem (prefilled)
Cost preview updates when action toggles are selected (estimate shown as delta)
Handoff mode snapshots export a one-click postmortem link and attaches to incident thread
Prototype validated in 6 responder sessions with >= 80% success on key tasks (find last decision, trigger runbook)
decisions: Compact drawer (300-420px) chosen over modal to preserve timeline awareness — tradeoff: less vertical space for deep logs
Decision traces limited to 3 most recent items to reduce noise; full history available via 'expand'
Cost delta shown as conservative estimate using 95th-percentile billing profile to avoid underpromising
Primary action order: Runbook -> Route -> Trigger Playbook -> Capture Postmortem (based on researcher interviews)
comments: 2026-03-03 Priya Kaur: Low-fi wireframes uploaded to Figma. Emphasis on fast scanability and handoff export. Added microcopy suggestions for action confirmations.
2026-03-05 Arjun Patel (ENG): Reviewed and flagged API work — need an endpoint for preflight cost delta and the decision-trace payload. Filed ENG-89120 as dependency.
2026-03-06 Maya Chen: Ran early hallway tests with 4 SREs. They liked the one-click capture but wanted clearer signal that an action will create downstream API calls (confirmation modal needed).
2026-03-07 Keisha Brown (PM): Suggest adding 'confidence' tag on decisions (low/med/high) so handoffs can prioritize checks. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10 Design critique notes: reduce visual noise in the briefcase header, strengthen contrast on action buttons, and make postmortem capture editable before send.
2026-03-12 ENG feedback (Suhani Rao): We can surface cost delta but need rate-limited calls to avoid throttling during high alert fan-out. Suggest caching last cost snapshot per-incident.

2026-03-14 Maya Chen: Updated hi-fi prototype (link above). Ready for the 6-session usability run next week. Front-end spec PR opened for preliminary review. Marking this ticket In Review for design QA.
follow_up_tasks: Localization pass for action copy - DES-758843
Engineering implementation spike for cost preflight caching - ENG-90733
usability_notes: Test script: 1) Open briefcase from active alert; 2) Identify last decision and rationale; 3) Toggle Route-to-Fallback and verify cost delta; 4) Trigger Capture-Postmortem and confirm draft contents. Record time-to-complete and verbal think-aloud. Target 6 completed sessions.
risks: If the cost delta API is slow, responders may mistrust the briefcase during high-severity incidents. Mitigation: show cached 'last known' with timestamp and a lightweight spinner while fresh values load.
next_steps: Run the usability sessions (03/16-03/18), incorporate results, finalize annotations for ENG spike, and land the front-end spec PR ahead of engineering sprint planning.
notes_for_engineering: Payload shape expectations included in front-end spec PR. Use optimistic UI for action confirmation to avoid blocking responders; ensure each action logs an audit event for the incident. Consider rate-limited cost preflight and per-incident cache TTL=60s.
